title: Weakly associated primes of a reduced ring are minimal
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring which is reduced, meaning that $x^n=0$ for $x\in R$ and $n\geq1$ implies $x=0$. For $x\in R$ write $\operatorname{Ann}_R(x)=\{a\in R:ax=0\}$. Let $\operatorname{WeakAss}(R)$ be the set of weakly associated primes of $R$ [def-sc-weakly-associated-primes]: the prime ideals $\mathfrak p$ such that, for some $x\in R$, $\mathfrak p$ is minimal among the prime ideals containing $\operatorname{Ann}_R(x)$. Then $\operatorname{WeakAss}(R)$ is exactly the set of minimal prime ideals of $R$ (prime ideals containing no strictly smaller prime ideal). No Noetherianity or finiteness assumption on the minimal primes is imposed; for the zero ring both sets are empty.

proof.text:
Fix a prime $\mathfrak p$ and put $A=R_{\mathfrak p}$ and $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak pA$ as in [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. The fraction equality there shows that $A$ is reduced: if $(a/s)^n=0$ with $n\geq1$, some $u

otin\mathfrak p$ to be zero, impossible.

proof.text: Now suppose $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{WeakAss}(R)$. Apply (1)$\Rightarrow$(3) of [lem-sc-weakass-localization] with the $R$-module $M=R$. Its module localization $R_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] identifies with $A$ by $r/s\mapsto r/s$, with inverse the same fraction formula; the fraction relations and scalar action agree. Thus there is $x\in A$ such that $\sqrt{\operatorname{Ann}_A(x)}=\mathfrak m$. Here $\sqrt I=\{z:z^n\in I\text{ for some }n\geq1\}$. The ideal $\mathfrak m$ is proper by [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime].

source.place: Tag 0EMA, label lemma-reduced-weakly-ass-minimal, proof; localization criterion Tag 0566, label lemma-weakly-ass-local.

proof.text: Write $x=a/s$ with $s\notin\mathfrak p$. If $a\notin\mathfrak p$, then $s/a$ is its inverse, so $\operatorname{Ann}_A(x)=0$. Reducedness from step 1 gives $\sqrt0=0$, hence $\mathfrak m=0$. If $a\in\mathfrak p$, then $x\in\mathfrak pA=\mathfrak m=\sqrt{\operatorname{Ann}_A(x)}$, so $x^n\in\operatorname{Ann}_A(x)$ for some $n\geq1$. Thus $x^{n+1}=0$, and step 1 gives $x=0$. But then its annihilator and its radical are $A$, contradicting properness of $\mathfrak m$. Only the first case is possible; therefore $\mathfrak pA=0$.

source.place: Tag 0EMA, label lemma-reduced-weakly-ass-minimal, proof; localization criterion Tag 0566, label lemma-weakly-ass-local.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-primes-of-localization](1), primes of $R$ contained in $\mathfrak p$ correspond to primes of $A$, with $\mathfrak p$ corresponding to $\mathfrak pA=0$. Every such prime of $A$ contains zero, and inclusion preservation makes it contained in zero; it must equal zero. Injectivity of the correspondence gives $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak p$ for every prime $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak p$. Thus $\mathfrak p$ is minimal. Conversely, if $\mathfrak p$ is any minimal prime of $R$, then $\operatorname{Ann}_R(1)=0$, so $1$ witnesses $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{WeakAss}(R)$ by [def-sc-weakly-associated-primes]. These two inclusions prove equality. In the zero ring there are no proper prime ideals, so both sets are empty.
